stem: A parent asks why a clinician is concerned about terminal complement deficiency (C5-C9) after repeated Neisseria infections; which explanation is most accurate?

options.text: These proteins are needed to form the membrane attack complex that lyses Neisseria
These proteins are required to produce all immunoglobulins
These proteins are necessary for neutrophil oxidative burst
These proteins primarily maintain lymphocyte numbers on the full blood count
These proteins prevent all autoimmune disease in childhood

explanation: Terminal complement deficiency means reduced formation of the membrane attack complex, which is important for lysing Neisseria and explaining recurrent Neisserial infections.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Infectious Disease in Childhood: Global and Regional Perspective

rationale: C5-C9 are terminal complement proteins that assemble the membrane attack complex; impaired MAC formation increases susceptibility to Neisseria.

optionExplanations.A: Correct because C5-C9 form the membrane attack complex, which lyses Neisseria and helps explain recurrent Neisserial infections.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because immunoglobulin production is a function of B cells, not terminal complement proteins.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because neutrophil oxidative burst is a separate antimicrobial mechanism and is not the role of C5-C9.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because lymphocyte numbers are not maintained by terminal complement proteins on the full blood count.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because terminal complement proteins do not prevent all autoimmune disease in childhood.

sourceRefs: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
